name: Jiuzi Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Jiuzi Holdings, Inc. is a Cayman Islands-incorporated micro-cap headquartered in Hangzhou, China, originally engaged in franchising and operating 'Jiuzi'-branded new energy vehicle (NEV) retail stores in lower-tier Chinese cities. Since 2025 it has pivoted toward a board-authorized crypto-asset treasury policy of up to $1 billion and an AI intelligent imaging and data platform, under CEO and Chairman Hongye Zhang (appointed May 2026). The company remains deeply loss-making with minimal cash, and FY2025 (ended October 31, 2025) revenue was $2.88M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Innovation Track Record (0/3): Revenue fell from $9.54M in FY2021 to $2.88M in FY2025, and the pivots into crypto treasury and AI imaging have not produced a proven new revenue stream [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): The company has announced an AI intelligent imaging and data platform and an intended AI cooperation agreement targeting ~$1.55M of profit contribution, but as of July 2026 the agreement was unsigned and no AI revenue was reported [4][5]. Market Share Leadership (0/2): Jiuzi is a sub-scale NEV franchisor with no share leadership in China's EV retail market. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management says the AI imaging platform is nearing commercialization, without named launch dates or revenue visibility [5]. R&D Intensity (0/1): The FY2025 income statement shows zero R&D spending [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Public materials describe green mobility and now AI and crypto ambitions, which read as boilerplate and shift with each strategic pivot [3][6]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): The CEO changed in April-May 2026 (Tao Li succeeded by Hongye Zhang), alongside a new COO and an auditor change, which signals instability rather than retention [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No open-market insider buying was found; capital has come from private placements [6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated on the Growth-sleeve formula; forward P/E and forward PEG were unavailable and excluded (7 weight units). D/E of 0.7% scores 1.00 and reported YoY revenue growth of 630% scores 1.00, though the growth comes off a tiny base [7]. ROE of -57.2% (2x weight) and a -251.5% profit margin score 0. The FY2021-FY2025 revenue CAGR of -25.9% (derived over four years from $9.54M to $2.88M because FY2020 data was unavailable) scores 0 at 2x weight [2]. That gives 2.0/7 = 2.86, rounded to 3. Liquidity barely clears the floor: 1.02M average shares x $1.09 = ~$1.11M/day, while recent volume of ~122K shares implies only ~$133K/day [7].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): The legacy business of franchising physical NEV retail stores in lower-tier Chinese cities is not directly replaceable by AI, but it is an intermediary model exposed to online and direct-to-consumer sales and to China's EV price war [1][2]. The company's survival now rests on speculative AI imaging and crypto initiatives whose partners analysts criticize as opaque [5][8]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI revenue has been reported; the AI cooperation agreement was still unsigned [4].

infinite_game.summary: Jiuzi is playing a pure survival game. It has cycled from EV franchising to a $1B crypto treasury policy to AI imaging within about two years, with leadership turnover and private placements along the way. Sinek would see no Just Cause here, only finite moves to sustain the listing and the share price.

just_cause.analysis: No enduring cause is evident; the stated purpose has moved from green mobility to crypto treasury to AI imaging within about two years [3][6]. Strategy follows market narratives rather than a vision of a better future.

trusting_teams.analysis: The CEO and Chairman changed in April-May 2026, a new COO with a blockchain background was appointed, and the auditor changed in 2026 [3]. The company has only ~33 employees, and there is no evidence of a stable, high-trust culture.

worthy_rivals.analysis: No commentary acknowledging competitors or learning from them was found. Communication centers on headline-grabbing announcements such as the $1B crypto policy [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: The company has changed its business model substantially, moving away from NEV retail toward AI imaging and digital assets [4][6]. The shifts are driven by financial desperation rather than a cause, which is why it earns only partial credit.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Headline capital commitments (up to $1B in crypto) dwarf the company's resources, and a delayed FY2024 20-F filing points to governance strain rather than principled long-term bets [6][8]. No sacrifice of near-term results for long-term capability is evident.

investment_thesis: Jiuzi is a speculative micro-cap whose legacy NEV franchising business has shrunk from $9.5M revenue in FY2021 to $2.9M in FY2025, with a -251% profit margin and a -57% ROE [2][7]. Recent revenue growth of 630% comes off a tiny base and has not translated into profitability, with a Q2 2026 net loss of $6.6M [1].
thesis_continued: The equity story now depends on unproven AI imaging and crypto treasury initiatives announced alongside leadership turnover, an auditor change and private placements [3][4][6]. Daily traded value of ~$1.1M barely clears IOWN's liquidity floor and recent volume is far below it, so the stock is not investable under the IOWN framework [7].
key_catalysts: Signing and commercialization of the AI intelligent imaging cooperation, which management guides could contribute ~$1.55M of profit [4][5]
Deployment of private-placement capital under the crypto-asset investment policy, which could re-rate the shares speculatively [6]
Continued revenue growth after reported YoY growth of 630% [7]
key_risks: Persistent heavy losses (FY2025 net loss of $10.2M on $2.88M revenue) and minimal cash [2]
Governance red flags: CEO turnover, an auditor change and a delayed FY2024 20-F filing [3][8]
Illiquidity and dilution risk from repeated private placements; recent daily traded value is well under $1M [7]
